solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What unlucky traveller may lose two legal actions?

definitions.meaning: luggage lost in transit, a bag a passenger might never see again
a suit and a case are both lawsuits, so the word splits into two court actions

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a luckless traveller might lose, seemingly framed in legal terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two legal actions' supplies both halves: SUIT and CASE are each a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage goes missing at airports, and a travel bag is just the thing an unlucky passenger loses.

clue.text: Smirk from MP is upsetting the Queen

indicators.note: upsetting means the letters of MP is are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A politician's smug look annoys the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly, self-satisfied smile is a near synonym of a smirk.

clue.text: Wrong corner — it bends around college

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the college abbreviation
bends means the letters of corner it are twisted into a new shape

explanation.surface: A street corner where the road curves round a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistaken or untrue is simply a synonym for wrong.

clue.text: Look under church pew

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Peering beneath a church bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pew' is informal British for a seat, as in 'take a pew', not only a church bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Take a pew is British slang for sit down, so a pew is any seat.

clue.text: Hot drink might have been moved

definitions.meaning: tea or coffee has the sugar mixed in with a spoon

explanation.surface: A cup of tea that may have been shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink mixed with a spoon, and feelings roused, share the same past participle.

clue.text: Pro golfer's first round — tee left behind

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for

indicators.note: first here asks for the opening letter of the word golfer's

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
tee is the name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A professional golfer's opening round, with a tee abandoned on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' is not a professional but the Latin-derived 'for', as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: To have forgotten something is to have left it behind, an idiomatic equivalence.

clue.text: Tories we ordered to capture hearts — or else!

indicators.note: to capture means the shuffled letters close around another piece
ordered means the letters of Tories we are rearranged

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A threat to the Conservatives to win over voters' hearts, or face the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meaning if not, or in a different way, is a straight equivalent of this adverb.

clue.text: People supporting good breeding

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the people word beneath the good letter

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: People backing selective breeding programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Refinement and polished manners are what good upbringing gives, both senses of elegance.

clue.text: Adore fund manager? Not quite

indicators.note: Not quite means the fund manager word stops one letter short

parts.note: a treasurer manages an organisation's funds

explanation.surface: Loving the person who runs the money, but only nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish or prize someone dearly is a close synonym for adore.

clue.text: Miles before chicane, broken down — one's help's required

indicators.note: broken down says the letters of chicane are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A car breaks down a mile before a racing chicane, and help is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' rearranges CHICANE into ECHANIC, while also setting the scene that makes the definition fit.
explanation.definitionFit: When a vehicle breaks down, the person whose assistance is needed is the repair specialist at the garage.

clue.text: Couch wears out, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals something heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: cloth that wears out frays

explanation.surface: A sofa getting threadbare, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couch' is the verb meaning to express in words, not the sofa; FRAYS said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch an idea is to word it in a particular way, a literary verb sense.

clue.text: Frank regularly seen after work

indicators.note: after places those picked letters behind the work abbreviation

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: A man called Frank turning up at work on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective for candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone candid and honest, hiding nothing, is frank.

clue.text: Dread removing top, revealing boob

indicators.note: removing top means the first letter of the word for dread is taken off

parts.note: dread is great fear, terror

explanation.surface: A fear of losing one's top and revealing a breast, a wardrobe-malfunction picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boob' is British slang for a blunder, not the anatomical sense the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal British slang for a silly mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Sign of hesitation over drinks for journalists

indicators.note: over in a crossword means turned back, so the hesitation word is reversed

parts.note: er is the sound people make when hesitating
porter is a dark beer, so porters are drinks

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating over a round of drinks for the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses ER to RE; porter is a dark stout-like beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper people who write the stories are another word for journalists.

clue.text: Let student calm down, initially

parts.note: L for learner, the plate on a British learner driver's car
to calm someone is to ease them

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word down

explanation.surface: Allowing a student to settle down, at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' is the past tense of renting out, not 'allow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A property that has been let has been rented out to a tenant, the same as hired out.

clue.text: Hide from Jacob?

parts.note: Jacob is a breed of spotted sheep, and a hide is an animal pelt; the surface suggests hiding from a man named Jacob

explanation.surface: Someone avoiding a person named Jacob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' is a noun, the pelt, and Jacob is a breed of sheep; there is also a nod to Jacob wearing animal skins to fool Isaac in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of a Jacob, a woolly farm animal breed, is the skin with its fleece on.

clue.text: One squeezing bottom? On the contrary — not at all!

indicators.note: squeezing means one piece holds another inside it
On the contrary flips the roles, so it is the bottom that squeezes the one

parts.note: nether means lower or bottom, as in nether regions
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about pinching someone's behind, firmly denied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses who squeezes whom: I goes inside NETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a negative, as in 'nor I, either', the word means also not, so not at all in either case.

clue.text: Delayed hospital diets and ate nuts

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of diets and ate go wild

explanation.surface: A hospital patient on a diet who ate nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food eaten but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing before acting, being slow to commit, is to have delayed.

clue.text: Stress certain to follow Trump, shortly?

indicators.note: to follow puts the certain word after the shortened title
shortly means the title is abbreviated to its first four letters

parts.note: Donald Trump is the US president
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Is stress bound to follow Donald Trump soon?
explanation.walkthrough: Pres is the usual short form for president.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain or tension weighing on someone is a near synonym of stress.

clue.text: Again cure Den?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to cure an illness is to treat it

explanation.surface: A question whether one might heal a den again.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a private hideaway, a place one withdraws to for quiet.

clue.text: Blast up and down?

definitions.note: a blast on a horn is a hoot, and the word for it is the same read upwards or downwards

indicators.note: up and down says the word reads the same both ways in this down entry

parts.note: a blast on a horn is a hoot, and the word for it is the same read upwards or downwards

explanation.surface: A horn sounding up and down a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A short blast on a car horn or a trumpet is a hoot.

clue.text: Worried, used any manoeuvres to remove Democrat

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters of used any are moved around
to remove says one letter is taken out of the pool before rearranging

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: An anxious politician who used every trick to oust a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D out of USEDANY and rearrange the remaining USEANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling anxious and ill at ease is a straightforward synonym for worried.

clue.text: Trunk now needs locks concealed

indicators.note: locks means the letters are shut away inside the words trunk now needs

explanation.surface: A trunk now has to have its locks covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' is a verb here, holding the answer inside, not the noun for fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden from view is not known, a loose sense of secret.

clue.text: Peaceful mountain climbing by detectives

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the mountain word reads upwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives calmly scaling a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and untroubled, without agitation, is a synonym for peaceful.

clue.text: Clippings go in this garbage bag

parts.note: scrap is waste or rubbish
to bag a seat is to book or reserve it

explanation.surface: Garden clippings tossed into a rubbish sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clippings' looks like hedge trimmings but means newspaper cuttings; 'bag' is a verb meaning reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper cuttings are pasted into an album kept for keepsakes and memorabilia.

clue.text: Embarrassed I had again finished

parts.note: an embarrassed face goes red
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone blushes, having finished the job a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Did the job once more, completing it a second time, is a re- verb in the past tense.

clue.text: Little child with a large sum

parts.note: a tot is a toddler
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A small child holding a big amount of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole amount when figures are added together is the overall sum.

clue.text: Argument from the setter of this crossword

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A dispute coming from the compiler of this very puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argument' means a subject or thesis, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The argument of a work is its central subject or topic.

clue.text: In an excited state, ditch novelist

parts.note: being up means being lively or excited
a dike (dyke) is a ditch or channel

explanation.surface: Someone in a frenzy dumps a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' is a noun here, a drainage channel, not a verb meaning dump.
explanation.definitionFit: John Updike was the American writer of the Rabbit novels.

clue.text: Before it's turned cold, head home

indicators.note: Before places the head word ahead of the rest

parts.note: dome is slang for the head

indicators.note: turned means the letters of it's are read backwards

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Heading home before the weather turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ITS to STI; 'home' is adjectival, as in home affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Home affairs are internal affairs of a country, so as an adjective home means internal or national.

clue.text: Being inclined to ignore leader's conclusion

indicators.note: to ignore leader's means dropping the first letter of the word for being inclined

parts.note: tending means being inclined to do something

explanation.surface: A tendency to disregard what the boss concluded.
explanation.definitionFit: The finish or last part of a story is its conclusion.

clue.text: At home, looked after fiancée

parts.note: being in means being at home
to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: A man caring for his bride-to-be at home.
explanation.definitionFit: One's future spouse is one's betrothed, a noun use of the word for planned.
